title: West End Roof and arriving by noisy sailboat
summary: Recollections of the West End Roof, where the interviewer's father played briefly, and Rau's noisy schooner arrivals that stopped the dancing.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Dad played out the West End Roof for a while, but it wasn't much longer than that he quit.

I don't think he played out there very long, no. I remember going out there on two or three occasions and sitting with them. But I never played much at that time. Most of my recollection of the West End Roof was coming in on a sailboat. They would, all the people would watch us coming in there. Because it made so damn much noise. Did you ever go to Agnes Boathouse out there? I had a friend who had a boat called Backe. He had a schooner. He had a two-cylinder engine that made enough noise you could hear it across Mandeville. All the people on the West End Roof would quit dancing to come watch us come in there because it made so damn much noise.
